title: English File Pre-Intermediate, File 11: used to, might, so and neither

fixIt.text: I use to play football when I was a child.
fixIt.explain: Used to for the past.

fixIt.text: Did you used to have long hair?
fixIt.explain: After did: use to, not used to.

fixIt.text: She might comes tomorrow.
fixIt.explain: Might + base form.

fixIt.text: I love dancing. So am I.
fixIt.explain: Love is a normal verb, so: So do I.

fixIt.text: When I was young, I use to swim in the river every day.
fixIt.explain: For past habits: used to + verb. In questions and negatives: did … use to.

fixIt.text: We didn't used to have a phone at home.
fixIt.explain: After didn't, use the base form: didn't use to.

fixIt.text: Did your father use to working in Battambang?
fixIt.explain: use to + verb: use to work.

fixIt.text: My grandmother used to living in a wooden house.
fixIt.explain: used to + verb (live), not -ing.

fixIt.text: I didn't use to liking vegetables, but now I love them.
fixIt.explain: use to + verb: didn't use to like.

fixIt.text: There use to be a big tree in front of our house.
fixIt.explain: There used to be = there was, but not now.

fixIt.text: My parents used to worked on a farm.
fixIt.explain: used to + verb: used to work.

fixIt.text: Take an umbrella. It might rains later.
fixIt.explain: might + verb with no -s: it might rain.

fixIt.text: I might going to the party, I'm not sure.
fixIt.explain: might + verb: I might go.

fixIt.text: She may not comes to class today.
fixIt.explain: may not + verb: she may not come.

fixIt.text: Sokha might is at the market.
fixIt.explain: might + be: she might be at the market.

fixIt.text: I'm tired. So do I.
fixIt.explain: Answer with the same verb: I'm tired. So am I.

fixIt.text: I can't swim. Neither do I.
fixIt.explain: Same verb as the first sentence: can't, so Neither can I.

fixIt.text: I went to Kep last year. So was I.
fixIt.explain: For the past simple, use did: So did I.

fixIt.text: I don't eat meat. So do I.
fixIt.explain: After a negative sentence, agree with Neither: Neither do I.

fixIt.text: I'm not hungry. Neither is I.
fixIt.explain: With I, use am: Neither am I.

builder.text: I used to live in the countryside.
I don't like coffee. Neither do I.
I used to live in Kampot.
builder.tip: used to + verb: a past habit or state.

builder.text: Did you use to play football?
builder.tip: Questions: Did you use to + verb?

builder.text: We didn't use to have a car.
I love mangoes. So do I.
builder.tip: Agree with So + the same helper verb + I.

radio.title: When I was a child
radio.text: When I was a child, we used to live in a village near Takeo. There used to be no electricity in the evenings, so we didn't use to watch TV. My brother and I used to play by the river after school. Now the village has a road and a market, and my parents might move back there next year. My father says he might grow mangoes again. I don't think I would like to live there again, but I love visiting.
